question.text: This pope, who served during World War II, has been called "Hitler's Pope" for not doing enough to stop the Holocaust.
question.clue: While on trial, Karl Wolff testified that he had been ordered to kidnap this leader, who gave a "Christmas Broadcast" in support of one group who had "been consigned to death or to a slow decline".

swap.text: Three members of the House of Medici went on to hold this office in Rome, taking the names Leo X, Clement VII, and Leo XI.
swap.answerHtml: Pope [or “the papacy;” or Supreme Pontiff; or Pontifex Maximus; or Bishop of Rome]
swap.clue: This position was subject to increased noble control during the pornocracy, and the last English holder of this position was Nicholas Breakspear.

question.leadin: Due to their military-like structure, members of this group are sometimes called "God's Marines."
question.text: Name this Catholic religious order founded by Ignatius Loyola. Members of this group included Francis Xavier, who traveled to Japan as a missionary.
question.clue: Two members of this group prepared the translation of the Treaty of Nerchinsk and another created a lunisolar calendar for the last Ming emperor.

swap.leadin: This term sometimes refers to the period of antipopes during the Avignon Papacy.
swap.text: Name this term which also applies to an exile of Jews from Judah begun by Nebuchadnezzar and ended by Cyrus the Great.
swap.clue: This period in which Philip IV of France moved the Papacy to Avignon, named after a duration of time in the Old Testament.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the investiture controversy.
question.text: The controversy over appointing bishops was sparked by the reforms launched by the seventh pope of this name. The thirteenth pope of this name created the modern calendar.
question.clue: Those two theologians with this name are from Nyssa and Nazianzus, and are considered "Cappadocian fathers" along with Basil the Great.

swap.leadin: Debate persists whether the slogan "God wills it" is appropriately attributed to this pope.
swap.text: Name this pope credited with inciting the First Crusade at the conclusion of the Council of Clermont in 1095.
swap.answerHtml: Pope Urban II [prompt on "Odo de Lagery"; or "Otto de Lagery"; or "Otho de Lagery"; or "Eudes de Lagery"]
swap.clue: This pope allied himself with Roger I of Sicily, and he was heavily influenced by a delegation sent by Alexius I Komnenos.

question.leadin: Terrorists planned to assassinate this pope during a visit to the Philippines in the first phase of the Bojinka Plot.
question.text: Name this pope who established World Youth Day in 1985. This pope's visit to his home country motivated the formation of the Solidarity movement, which went on to end communist rule in that country.
question.clue: This man officially condemned Liberation Theology, and he unofficially supported the Solidarity movement in his home country.

swap.leadin: French religion has been continually chaotic throughout history.
swap.text: Seven successive popes resided in this French prefecture rather than in Rome during the "Babylonian captivity of the Papacy."
swap.clue: This city was called "a sewer where all the muck of the universe collects" by Petrarch, who coined an enduring Biblical nickname for it.

question.leadin: Moderator note: do not read the alternate answers to the first part. Stefan Zweig characterized a commander of this organization named Nicolas Durand de Villegaignon as a "half-pirate, half-scientist."
question.text: Name this military order founded by Italian merchants from Amalfi in 11th century Jerusalem to care for sick and poor pilgrims.
question.answerHtml: Knights Hospitaller [or the Order of Saint John of Jerusalem or Order of the Hospital of Saint John of Jerusalem or Sovereign Military and Hospitaller Order of Saint John of Jerusalem, of Rhodes, and of Malta; accept Order of Malta]
question.clue: This group, founded by the Blessed Gerard, controlled the fortresses of Margat (mar-GAH) and Krak des Chevaliers ("crack" deh sheh-val-YAY) before it was forced from the Holy Land.

swap.leadin: It followed the ineffectual rule of Benedict XI.
swap.text: Name this period officially lasting from 1309 to 1377 that was resolved in the Council of Constance, in which several popes generally took up residence in a certain French city.
swap.clue: The man who ended this time period did so after reading a letter written by Catherine of Siena.

question.leadin: Identify the following about a church council.
question.text: Called for the purpose of ending the Great Schism, this 1414 council compelled all three competing popes to withdraw and elected Martin V.

swap.leadin: Hundreds of members of this group were arrested on October 13, 1307, which may have contributed to the idea that Friday the 13th is unlucky.
swap.text: Name this group whose leader Jacques de Molay was burned at the stake on the orders of Philip IV of France and Pope Clement V, who regarded this group as a bunch of heretics; both Clement and Philip died less than a year later.
swap.answerHtml: Knights Templar [or Templars; or Order of Solomon's Temple; or Poor Fellow-Soldiers of Christ and of the Temple of Solomon]
swap.clue: Members of this rival to the Hospitallers were purchased and executed en masse by Saladin after he won the Battle of Hattin.

question.text: The fifth pope to take this name suppressed the Templars at the Council of Vienne and moved the papacy to Avignon, thus beginning the Babylonian Captivity.
question.clue: He rescinded an earlier papal bull which proclaimed that outside of the church, there is no salvation.

swap.text: On his flight back from a trip to Rio de Janeiro, Francis affirmed homosexual orientation is not itself a sin. He then considered the example of a gay person seeking God, and asked this question. It's usually rendered as five or six words in English.
swap.answerHtml: “Who am I to judge [him]?” or “Chi sono io per giudicarlo?”

question.text: Excavations in the 1930s discovered that the Castra Nova of the equites singulares was well preserved under this oldest public Roman church. This church, the cathedral of Rome, as well as a nearby palace take their name from the estate of the family which included the first plebeian to become consul.

swap.text: During his war with Philip II over Normandy, John attempted to secure assistance from this pope. This pope convoked the Fourth Lateran Council and called for the Fourth Crusade.
swap.answerHtml: Pope Innocent III [or Innocentius III ; accept Lotario dei Conti di Segni or Lothar of Segni ; prompt on Pope Innocent or Innocentius ]
swap.clue: This pope placed England under interdict after John chose the Bishop of Norwich, John de Grey, over Stephen Langton as Archbishop of Canterbury.

question.text: This unrecognized 1409 council attempted to sort out the Western Schism by deposing both Benedict and Gregory, but fucked up by electing the compromise pope Alexander V.
question.clue: It was presided over by the Bishop of Palestrina, and came to a climax with a stirring denunciation delivered by Simon de Cramaud, the Patriarch of Alexandria, after which Baldassare Cossa successfully intrigued on behalf of Peter Philarghi.

swap.text: Martin Luther used jester's privilege when he suggested that monks should break their chastity vows in one of his polemics in response to this document, which he then burned, leading to his excommunication a year later.
swap.answerHtml: Exsurge Domine [or Arise, O Lord] (That polemic is Address to the Nobility of the German Nation.)
swap.clue: Some of the specific claims this document notes as especially problematic include: "A good work very well done is a venial sin," and "Christians must be taught to cherish excommunications rather than to fear them."

question.leadin: Michaelist sources, such as The Chronicle of Nicholas the Minorite, were cited as proof of the intransigency of this Pope during the Apostolic Poverty Controversy. FTPE.
question.text: Name this Pope during the Avignon Papacy who succeeded Clement V in 1316. He quarreled with Emperor Louis IV of Bavaria, who under advice of William of Ockham, set up the antipope Nicholas V.

swap.text: The 325 Council of Nicaea was called during the tenure of this pope, who was also gifted vast amounts of land and power by the forged Donation of Constantine.
swap.clue: He supposedly cured the leprosy of an emperor who built the original Basilica of St. Peter's.
